title: Hrithik Roshan Flies to Chennai for Jailer 2. Forty Years After His Debut, the Child Actor Returns to Rajinikanth's Side.
excerpt: Shah Rukh Khan walked away over a scheduling clash with 'King.' What the makers found instead is a reunion four decades in the making — and a never-before-seen avatar the Greek God says he's never tried.
body:
The picture leaked before the press note did. A grainy frame from a Chennai airport, a familiar jawline under a cap, and within an hour the Tamil film internet had done the math: **Hrithik Roshan** was in town, and there was only one reason a Bollywood A-lister quietly slips into Chennai in late June 2026. **Jailer 2** had found its big cameo.

Variety India confirmed it after weeks of whispers — Hrithik will shoot his portions in **Rajinikanth's** sequel on June 22 and 23, undergoing multiple look tests for an avatar the makers describe as entirely new, something his fans have never seen on him. And here is the detail that turns a casting scoop into something genuinely lovely: this is not the first time these two have shared a frame. It is the second. The first was forty years ago.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=Hy2nbw57O78</youtube>


In 1986, a wide-eyed child named Hrithik Roshan made his acting debut in *Bhagwaan Dada*, playing the foster son of a character played by a young Rajinikanth. The Superstar was already a phenomenon down south; the boy was the grandson of the film's director. Hrithik has told the story many times since, and it never loses its warmth.



> **"This happened every single time so that I, a child, would not get conscious." — Hrithik Roshan, on working with Rajinikanth in 1986

That is the kind of anecdote that ages into legend."**


https://x.com/Girish__28/status/2069317743304937557


![Chennai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/32/Chennai_Central.jpg)


> "Whenever I messed up a shot, my grandfather used to cut the shot, and Rajini sir used to take the blame. He would say, 'Sorry, my fault,' but it was actually my fault. This happened every single time so that I, a child, would not get conscious." — Hrithik Roshan, on working with Rajinikanth in 1986

That is the kind of anecdote that ages into legend. The boy who was protected on set by the biggest star in the room is now one of Hindi cinema's most bankable leading men, walking back onto a Rajinikanth set as an equal. Forty years is a long time to wait for a second take.

The road here was not straight. For months the cameo was earmarked for **Shah Rukh Khan**, who had reportedly agreed to shoot for five days. Then the calendar got in the way. With *Jailer 2* slated to land before SRK's own comeback vehicle **King**, Khan reportedly balked at being seen in any look before his own film unveiled it — a very King-sized concern — and stepped away. The makers pivoted to Hrithik, and somehow the consolation prize became the better story.

Director **Nelson Dilipkumar** built the first *Jailer* into a 2023 monster partly on the strength of its cameos — a parade of pan-Indian icons dropped into Muthuvel Pandian's world like grenades. The sequel is stacking the bench even higher. Alongside Rajinikanth, the ensemble reportedly includes **Mohanlal**, **Shiva Rajkumar**, **Vijay Sethupathi**, **Mithun Chakraborty**, **Vidya Balan** (making her full Tamil debut), SJ Suryah and Ramya Krishnan, with **Anirudh Ravichander** scoring and **Sun Pictures** producing. Hrithik's sequence, sources say, arrives at a crucial hinge in the plot, where his character aids Rajinikanth and pushes the story forward — mounted, naturally, on a grand scale.

For Hrithik, this is his first new commitment since *War 2* in August 2025, and his first proper dance with South Indian cinema at the height of the pan-India era. The man can move, he can brood, and he photographs like a sculpture — the idea of that physicality dropped into a Rajinikanth mass moment is the sort of thing that makes a single-screen crowd lose its mind. If he and the Superstar genuinely share the frame in full flight, theatres are looking at one of the loudest whistle-worthy beats in recent memory.

For the diaspora, *Jailer 2* is the easy part. The first film was a worldwide event for Sun Pictures, and the sequel — reportedly eyeing a September 11 release before a possible slide into Diwali — will roll out in Tamil, Telugu, Hindi, Kannada and Malayalam across the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf, with the kind of Friday-first-show fan screenings that turn New Jersey and Edison multiplexes into Chennai for a night. Expect it to stream eventually, but this is not a couch film. This is a film you see with two hundred strangers screaming.

No official word yet from the makers, who, true to *Jailer* form, neither confirm nor deny. They don't have to. The photo already did. Forty years on, the kid is back on set with the man who took the blame for him — and this time, nobody's cutting the shot.
